name: Absolute Pin
definition: A piece is pinned to the King along a rank, file, or diagonal. It is illegal for the pinned piece to move because doing so would expose the King to check.
tactical_cue: Look for an enemy King aligned behind an enemy piece on an open file or diagonal with a Rook, Bishop, or Queen.
remedy_advice: Step the King off the danger diagonal, interpose a defending piece, or add defense to the pinned piece before the opponent attacks it again with a pawn.

name: Relative Pin
definition: A piece is pinned to a higher-value piece (such as the Queen or Rook). Moving the pinned piece is legal but typically causes fatal material loss.
tactical_cue: Unprotected Queen or Rook standing behind a minor piece or pawn on an open diagonal or file.
remedy_advice: Move the higher-value piece away, break the pin with a counter-attack with check, or neutralize the pinning piece.

name: Knight Fork
definition: A single Knight attacks two or more valuable enemy pieces simultaneously (often King + Queen or King + Rook).
tactical_cue: Two enemy pieces sitting on squares of the same color, separated by 2-3 squares where a Knight can land safely (e.g. c7, c2, f7, f2).
remedy_advice: Never leave heavy pieces on the same square color within jumping range of an active enemy knight. Control key outpost squares.

name: Pawn Fork
definition: An advancing pawn simultaneously threatens two enemy minor pieces on adjacent diagonal squares.
tactical_cue: Two enemy minor pieces resting on adjacent files on the same rank (e.g., c6 and e6 or c3 and e3).
remedy_advice: Ensure minor pieces are not laterally placed without escape squares when an enemy pawn advance (like d4 or d5) can split them.

name: Skewer
definition: An attack on a high-value piece (like King or Queen) that forces it to move aside, exposing a lower-value piece behind it to capture.
tactical_cue: A valuable piece standing directly in front of another piece on an open rank, file, or diagonal.
remedy_advice: Step the valuable piece to a square that simultaneously defends the piece behind it, or counter-attack with check.

name: Discovered Attack & Check
definition: Moving a piece unmasks a hidden line of attack from a friendly Queen, Rook, or Bishop against an enemy target.
tactical_cue: A friendly piece standing directly in the line between your long-range piece and an enemy piece or King.
remedy_advice: Move your targeted piece away or eliminate the unmasking piece immediately before it jumps with devastating tempo.

name: Deflection (Overloaded Defender)
definition: Forcing an enemy piece to leave its defensive post so that another square, piece, or checkmate path becomes undefended.
tactical_cue: A key enemy piece burdened with defending two critical squares or pieces at once.
remedy_advice: Add a second defender to the overloaded square, or simplify by trading off the attacking pieces.

name: Back-Rank Weakness
definition: A King trapped behind its own shield of pawns (e.g., f7-g7-h7 or f2-g2-h2) on the 1st or 8th rank delivered checkmate by a Rook or Queen.
tactical_cue: Castled King with no 'luft' (escape square) and few defenders on the back rank.
remedy_advice: Create 'luft' by advancing h3/g3 or ...h6/...g6 early. Keep at least one heavy piece or minor piece guarding the back rank.

name: Trapped Piece
definition: A piece that has wandered into enemy territory and has all its legal escape squares covered or captured.
tactical_cue: Minor piece (especially bishop or knight) venturing deep into the opponent's flank without friendly pawn support (e.g. Bishop on a7 or a2).
remedy_advice: Always maintain an escape retreat square or pawn break before committing pieces behind enemy lines.

name: Decoy / Attraction
definition: Sacrificing a piece to lure an enemy piece (usually the King) onto a square where it can be subjected to a fatal tactic.
tactical_cue: Luring an enemy piece onto a square that sets up a fork, skewer, or mating net.
remedy_advice: Carefully calculate forcing moves and sacrifices before accepting free poisoned material.
